name: Sorrel Dey
title: Marshal
note: The colony's only lawkeeper. Easygoing, capable and quick to tell you that everything's under control.
appearance: A rangy woman with sun-cracked lips, a star cut from a ration tin pinned to her coat and a long rifle slung muzzle-down. She always looks as if she's just stopped walking, and an old dog she swears is her deputy looks the same.
personality: Easygoing, funny and worn through. Elder Dray raised her from an orphan, and she'd walk into a fire for her. She's the most honest person in the colony about everything but the one thing that matters, and she's lying to the one person she has never lied to.
voice: A slow, friendly drawl full of understatement. Everything is "a little bit of a situation" and "nothing to lose sleep over". Never uses the word "problem". Says "It's handled" while her hand goes to the rifle. A barn on fire would be "some smoke out by the east wells". The worse it is, the more relaxed she sounds, and people who know her have learned to be frightened when she starts smiling.
goals: Keep her son Emmet and the other children out of whatever's under the colony, and keep Elder Dray from finding out how far it's gone until she has an answer. She's running out of nights.
secrets: She has told Elder Dray it's six children speaking the strange language. It's thirty-one, nearly every child under twelve. They've begun walking in their sleep out to the Well-Head, all at the same hour, and for weeks she and the schoolteacher have been carrying them back to bed before dawn. The stone cap has cracked from below twice, and she repoured it herself. Her own son Emmet, who's eight, was the first, and the others learned it from him. She's lying because she knows what Dray would do: blast the chamber, or send the children away. She doesn't know which of those she fears more. When Tessaly Marsh came through two months ago and offered to take Emmet, Sorrel drew on her. She'll hint at the truth to anyone who has earned a little trust, and she'll give the real number if you ask her twice.

intro: "Now, this is a little bit of a situation," Sorrel Dey says, smiling, and unslings the long rifle.
hit: The rifle cracks, and something hits you very hard. "Sorry about that," she says, and she is.
She clips you with the rifle butt on her way past. "Just a little one."
miss: The shot goes by close enough to hear. "That was a warning," she says. It wasn't.
You dive, and the shot chews up the place you just left.
defeated: Sorrel Dey sits down and lays the rifle across her knees. "It's handled," she says, to nobody.
